description:
The orphan-leaf check compares a leaf issue's labels with the configured type names, not their membership label namespaces. It gives wrong results whenever a type's membership namespace differs from the type's name.

## Background

`HierarchyConfig::membership_namespaces()` yields `(type_name, namespace)` pairs from `label_associations` (`crates/jit/src/domain/type_taxonomy.rs:216-221`). `validate_orphans` destructures each pair as `(namespace, _)` (`crates/jit/src/domain/type_taxonomy.rs:445-450`). It binds the type name and discards the actual namespace. It then looks for labels prefixed `<type_name>:`.

When every association maps a type to a namespace of the same name (e.g. `epic -> epic`), the bug is invisible. With an association such as `release -> milestone`:

- a leaf labelled `milestone:v1` is reported as an orphaned leaf;
- a leaf labelled `release:v1` (a namespace no association declares) passes as having a parent.

Reproduction: configure `[type_hierarchy.label_associations] release = "milestone"` with `release` above a leaf type, then create a leaf-type issue labelled `milestone:v1` and validate. The issue is reported as an orphaned leaf.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A leaf-type issue that carries a label in any configured membership namespace raises no orphaned-leaf warning, including when that namespace differs from its associated type's name.
- [hard] REQ-02: A leaf-type issue whose only label prefix matches a type name, not a configured membership namespace, raises an orphaned-leaf warning.
- [hard] REQ-03: A regression test covers a type-to-namespace association whose names differ and asserts both outcomes above.

## Notes

The pair order is documented on `membership_namespaces`. `detect_membership_issues` in the same file already reads it correctly as `(type_name, namespace)`.
title: Orphan-leaf validation checks type names instead of membership namespaces
